name: Jeremiah
lede: The twenty-fourth book of the Bible, in full: the young prophet set over the nations, the potter's house and the yoke, the roll burned in the fire, the prophet in the dungeon, the fall of Jerusalem and the flight into Egypt, the burdens of the nations, and the promise of a new covenant, every word in the words of the ASV.

books.name: The Almond Rod
books.blurb: Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee — ah, Lord Jehovah! I know not how to speak, for I am a child; I have put my words in thy mouth; the rod of an almond-tree and the boiling caldron from the north; the kindness of thy youth; they have forsaken me, the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out broken cisterns; and return, O backsliding children.

books.name: Evil from the North
books.blurb: Blow ye the trumpet in the land, set up a standard toward Zion; a lion is gone up from his thicket; my anguish, my anguish! I beheld the earth, and, lo, it was waste and void; run ye to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem, if ye can find a man; peace, peace, when there is no peace; ask for the old paths; and a people cometh from the north country.

books.name: The Temple of Jehovah
books.blurb: Stand in the gate of Jehovah's house: trust ye not in lying words, the temple of Jehovah, the temple of Jehovah; is this house become a den of robbers?; go ye now unto Shiloh; cakes to the queen of heaven and the valley of Slaughter; the stork knoweth her appointed times; is there no balm in Gilead?; oh that my head were waters; and let him that glorieth glory in this, that he knoweth me.

books.name: The Broken Covenant
books.blurb: Learn not the way of the nations: they deck the tree with silver and with gold, and fasten it with nails; but Jehovah is the true God; my tent is destroyed; O Jehovah, correct me, but in measure; hear ye the words of this covenant; I was like a gentle lamb that is led to the slaughter; wherefore doth the way of the wicked prosper?; if thou hast run with the footmen, how canst thou contend with horses?

books.name: The Marred Girdle
books.blurb: A linen girdle hidden in a cleft of the rock by the Euphrates, and, behold, the girdle was marred; every bottle shall be filled with wine; can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots?; the drought, and the gates sitting in black; though Moses and Samuel stood before me; woe is me, my mother; thy words were found, and I did eat them; and a fortified brazen wall.
